item.description:
[Chapter 34] No Need to Get Angry at a Barking Dog ([34화] 짖는 개에게 화낼 필요는 없다)

☞ Start from Chapter 1 (☞ 1화부터 보기)

☞ Character Introductions (☞ 등장인물 소개)

Irina tightened her grip on Evan's hand as she retraced old memories. Outside the hospital window, Tokyo's nightscape blurred into haze. (이리나는 옛 기억을 되짚으며 에반의 손을 꽉 잡았다. 병실의 창밖으로 도쿄의 야경이 흐릿하게 번졌다.)

The stiff-backed man who once stood against three-to-one odds in London now lay asleep, wrapped in bandages, unable even to call Irina's name. (런던에서 3대1 앞에 서던 그 뻣뻣한 남자가, 지금은 붕대에 감긴 채 이리나의 이름도 부르지 못하고 잠들었다.)

The smell of antiseptic in the hospital room stirred Irina's old memories. The winter in Bucharest, the sounds heard through the walls, the wailing of her family, shattering plates, and the silence that came unexpectedly one day. (병실의 소독약 냄새가 이리나의 오래된 기억을 건드렸다. 부쿠레슈티의 겨울, 벽 너머로 들리던 소리들, 가족들의 울부짖음, 깨지는 접시, 그리고 어느 날 갑자기 찾아온 적막.)

The sound of the front door closing was her last memory of her father's retreating figure. (현관문이 닫히는 소리가 아버지의 뒷모습을 본 마지막 기억이었다.)

Twelve-year-old Irina couldn't tell whether that silence meant freedom or abandonment. She filled her mother's empty place by preparing her siblings' breakfasts, and after school she hauled loads at the market. That's when she learned her body had worth. (열두 살의 이리나는 그 적막이 자유를 얻은 것인지, 버려진 것인지 구분하지 못했다. 엄마의 빈자리를 채우듯 동생들의 아침을 차리고, 학교가 끝나면 시장에서 짐을 날랐다. 몸이 쓸모 있다는 걸 안 건 그 무렵이다.)

To protect her own family, she first had to learn how to fight back. That's how fighting became a livelihood, and the livelihood became a career. (제 식구를 지키려면, 맞서는 법을 먼저 배워야 했다. 그렇게 싸움은 생계가 됐고, 생계는 직업이 됐다.)

In Irina's memory, men left either wounds or empty spaces. There were no exceptions. But this man was neither. (이리나의 기억 속 남자들은 상처를 남기거나 빈자리를 남겼다. 예외는 없었다. 그런데 이 남자는 둘 다 아니었다.)

Evan's fingers twitched faintly in his sleep. Irina didn't let go of his hand. (에반의 손가락이 잠결에 미세하게 움직였다. 이리나는 그 손을 놓지 않았다.)

He couldn't even fight, yet he didn't run. Even while taking hits, he shielded Irina behind his back. I've protected others before, but no one has ever protected me. (싸움도 못 하면서 도망가지 않았다. 맞으면서도 이리나를 등 뒤로 감쌌다. 내가 누군가를 지켜준 적은 있지만, 누군가 나를 지켜준 적은 없으니까.)

A few weeks after Evan's accident in Tokyo, Vice President Patrick convened a sales strategy meeting. Even if a piece falls on the chessboard, the game goes on. (에반의 도쿄 사고 후 몇 주 후, 패트릭 부사장은 영업 전략 회의를 소집했다. 체스판의 말이 쓰러져도 게임은 계속되는 법.)

The clock at Dudael Tech raced forward like an arrow, with no time—or more precisely, no inclination—to worry about the wounded. (듀다엘 테크의 시계는 부상자를 신경 쓸 겨를도 없이, 아니 정확히는 신경도 쓰지 않은 채, 화살처럼 앞으로 나아갔다.)

Even before the meeting began, Patrick had put Dudael's sales performance data up on the large screen. This quarter's results were close to the finance team's guidance, but Patrick had no intention whatsoever of congratulating them on hitting their targets. Because the pinnacle of a vast organization isn't earned through performance or performance reviews alone. (패트릭은 회의가 시작하기도 전에 대형 스크린 화면에 듀다엘의 매출 현황 자료를 띄워놓았다. 이번 분기 실적은 재무팀 가이던스에 근접했지만, 패트릭은 목표 달성을 격려할 생각이 추호도 없었다. 거대 조직의 정점은, 실적이나 인사 평가로만 얻는 것이 아니기 때문이다.)

Inside the conference room, with external light blocked out, only the blue glow of the large display swirled. On the screen, the global status of Sariel contract negotiations flickered in red and yellow dots. (회의실 안은 외부의 빛이 차단된 공간에 대형 디스플레이의 청색광만 감돌았다. 화면에는 전 세계 사리엘 계약 추진 현황이 붉은색과 노란색 점으로 깜빡였다.)

When Patrick rose with his neck held straight, the low murmuring in the conference room fell silent. The executives swallowed dryly behind their shirt collars and studied Patrick's expression. (패트릭이 목을 곧게 세운 채로 일어서자, 회의실에서 낮게 웅성대던 소리가 사라졌다. 임원들은 셔츠 깃 뒤로 마른침을 삼키며 패트릭의 안색을 살폈다.)

Instead of taking the head seat, Patrick slowly circled the conference table. (패트릭은 상석에 앉는 대신 회의 테이블 주위를 천천히 돌았다.)

The rhythmic sound of his dress shoes striking the marble was chilling. Patrick's gaze stopped on Jeff Ballinger, who was attending this meeting for the first time. Jeff offered an awkward smile to hide his nerves. (구두 굽이 대리석에 부딪히는 규칙적인 소리가 공포감을 자아냈다. 패트릭의 시선이 이번 회의에 처음 참석한 제프 밸린저에게 멈췄다. 제프는 긴장을 감추려 어색한 미소를 지어 보였다.)

"What's your name?" (“이름이 뭐지?”)

"Jeff Ballinger. I was just transferred from the Korean branch to headquarters. It's an honor to be at this meeting." (“제프 밸린저입니다. 한국 지사에서 본사로 막 발령받았습니다. 이 자리에 참석하게 되어 영광입니다.”)

Patrick didn't return the smile. Instead, he looked Jeff over from shoulder to cuff. With two fingers, he lightly flicked the lapel of Jeff's suit. (패트릭은 미소를 돌려주지 않았다. 대신 제프의 어깨부터 소매 끝까지 훑었다. 두 손가락으로 제프의 수트 라펠을 가볍게 튕겼다.)

"How much did this suit cost?" (“이 옷은 얼마짜린가?”)

"Excuse me? Ah... I purchased it from Brooks Brothers." (“네? 아…… 브룩스 브라더스에서 구매한 것입니다만.")

"Brooks Brothers?" (“브룩스 브라더스?”)

A sneer curled at the corner of Patrick's mouth. The suit didn't matter. The name didn't matter either. The first person who takes a hit without fighting back becomes the sacrificial lamb of the conference room. (패트릭의 입가에 비웃음이 걸렸다. 옷은 상관없었다. 이름도 상관없었다. 맞고도 반격하지 않는 첫 번째 사람이, 회의실의 제물이 된다.)

"You're the man who sells the eyes of God worth hundreds of millions of dollars. And you stand before clients wearing mass-produced off-the-rack suits?" (“자네는 지금 수억 달러짜리 신의 눈을 팔러 다니는 사람이야. 그런데 대량 생산된 기성복을 걸치고 고객 앞에 선다고?”)

"I'll make sure to wear proper attire at meetings from now on." (“앞으로 회의엔 꼭 좋은 옷을 입고 오겠습니다.”)

"It's not in front of me—wearing proper attire in front of clients is the bare minimum!" (“내 앞에서가 아니라 고객들 앞에서 좋은 옷을 입는 건 기본 중의 기본이야!”)

Patrick's shout struck the ceiling. (패트릭의 고함이 천장을 때렸다.)

"Who would trust a system sold by a man who walks around in cheap clothes? You really have no fundamentals!" (“싸구려 옷을 입고 다니는 놈이 파는 시스템을 누가 신뢰하겠나? 정말이지 기본이 안 돼 있군!”)

Jeff bowed his head. The other executives, as if by unspoken agreement, fixed their eyes on the meeting materials. Patrick immediately pointed at the map on the screen. (제프는 고개를 숙였다. 다른 임원들은 약속이라도 한 듯 회의 자료로 시선을 박았다. 패트릭은 곧바로 화면 속 지도를 가리켰다.)

"What about the situation in Japan? Isn't this the point where signing a contract today wouldn't be out of line?" (“일본 상황은 어때? 여기는 오늘 당장 계약을 체결해도 이상하지 않은 시점 아닌가?”)

Jeff cleared his throat and picked up the briefing folder. It was to buy time. The other executives all dropped their heads at once. (제프가 헛기침을 하며 브리핑 폴더를 집어 들었다. 시간을 벌기 위해서였다. 다른 임원들은 일제히 고개를 떨궜다.)

"We're currently in close consultation with the Japanese government. Coordinating through multiple channels..." (“현재 일본 정부와 긴밀히 협의 중이라고 합니다. 여러 채널을 통해 조율을....”)

"In consultation?" Patrick cut Jeff off as if he'd been waiting for that exact word. (“협의 중?” 패트릭이 제프의 말을 기다렸다는 듯 잘랐다.)

"Next time you come, bring a signed contract instead of those words. Or bring your resignation." (“다음에 올 때는 그 말 대신 서명이 찍힌 계약서를 가져와. 아니면 사표를 들고 오든지.”)

Leaving Jeff's frightened face behind, Patrick's cold gaze moved to the person in charge of South America. (제프의 겁먹은 표정을 뒤로한 채 패트릭의 서늘한 시선이 남미 담당자에게 옮겨갔다.)

"What about South America?" (“남미 쪽은?”)

"We're examining from multiple angles whether to enter Peru or Chile first, considering the security conditions." (“페루와 칠레 중 어느 국가에 먼저 진출할지 안보 여건을 다각적으로 검토하고 있습니다.”)

Patrick slammed his fist on Chile's coastline on the map. (패트릭이 지도의 칠레 해안선을 주먹으로 내리쳤다.)

"Look at the length of Chile's border. Only a fool wouldn't know where Sariel's main market is. You're not sitting here to 'review.' Prove it with results, right now." (“칠레의 국경선 길이를 봐. 바보가 아닌 이상 어디가 사리엘의 주 시장인지 모를 수가 있나? 당신들은 여기서 검토나 하라고 앉아 있는 게 아니야. 당장 성과로 증명해.”)

Patrick strode out like a stage actor who'd just delivered his closing lines. No one moved until the sound of his shoes completely faded at the end of the hallway. (패트릭은 마치 대사를 끝낸 연극 배우처럼 자리를 박차고 나갔다. 구두 소리가 복도 끝에서 완전히 사라질 때까지 아무도 움직이지 않았다.)

Once in the private elevator, Patrick checked his appearance in the metal walls. The flush from shouting in the meeting had already returned to calm. (전용 엘리베이터에 올라탄 패트릭은 금속 벽면에 비친 자신의 매무새를 확인했다. 회의실 고함으로 달아올랐던 안색은 이미 평온을 되찾았다.)

He pulled out his smartphone and sent a short message. (주머니에서 스마트폰을 꺼내 짧은 메시지를 보냈다.)

The recipient was Alistair Carrington, the old-money tycoon who held Dudael's capital lifeline. (수신인은 앨리스터 캐링턴, 듀다엘의 자본 줄기를 쥐고 있는 올드 머니 거물.)

"Your plan may be able to move forward a little faster." (“당신의 계획이 조금 더 빨리 추진될 수 있을 겁니다.”)

Patrick's face, pressing the send button, was reflected coldly in the elevator walls. (전송 버튼을 누르는 패트릭의 얼굴이 엘리베이터 벽면에 차갑게 반사됐다.)

To him, a subordinate's humiliation was merely cheap fuel to accelerate business. (그에게 부하 직원의 수치심은 사업 속도를 높이기 위한 값싼 연료에 불과했다.)

Jeff was left alone in the empty conference room. He grabbed his suit sleeve roughly, then loosened his tie. There was only one way to recover the pride Patrick had trampled on: squeezing a weaker link than himself. (텅 빈 대회의실에 제프만 덩그러니 남았다. 수트 소매를 거칠게 움켜쥐었다가, 넥타이를 풀어 헤쳤다. 패트릭이 짓밟고 간 자존심을 회복할 방법은 하나뿐이었다. 자신보다 약한 고리를 쥐어짜는 것.)

Jeff picked up his smartphone and called Evan. It connected after two rings. (제프는 스마트폰을 집어 들어 에반에게 전화를 걸었다. 신호음 두 번 만에 연결됐다.)

"Yes, this is Evan." (“네, 에반입니다.”)

Evan's voice was businesslike. No pain, no fear in it. (에반의 목소리는 사무적이었다. 통증이나 두려움은 느껴지지 않았다.)

"You're not lying in your hospital bed watching Netflix, are you?" (“자네, 지금 병상에 누워서 넷플릭스나 보고 있을 때는 아닐 텐데?”)

Jeff's voice was sharp, mimicking Patrick's. The one who'd just been hit striking the next person—a common food chain in the defense industry. (제프의 목소리는 패트릭의 그것을 흉내 내듯 날카로웠다. 방금 맞은 자가 다음 사람을 때리는, 방산 업계에서 흔한 먹이사슬이었다.)

"Just tell me what you need." (“용건만 말씀하십시오.”)

"What? What I need?" (“뭐? 용건?”)

Jeff's brow twitched. (제프의 눈썹이 꿈틀거렸다.)

"What I need to hear from you isn't your hospital admission report—it's the Philippine Ministry of Defense contract!" (“내 귀에 들어와야 할 건 자네 병원 입원 보고가 아니라, 필리핀 국방부 계약서야!”)

Imagining himself as a tough guy, he kicked the chair awkwardly. (머릿속 터프한 모습을 그리며, 부자연스럽게 의자를 발로 걷어찼다.)

"Vice President Patrick is going crazy demanding results right now, and what are you doing over there? I told you last week to meet the defense ministry people and put pressure on them. Stop with that vague 'in consultation' nonsense and get the contract stamped right now." (“패트릭 부사장님이 지금 당장 성과를 가져오라고 난리인데 거기서 뭐 하고 있는 거야. 지난주에도 방위성 사람 만나서 압박하라고 했잖아. ‘협의 중’이라는 뜬구름 잡는 소리 말고 당장 계약서 도장 받아내.”)

"Understood." (“알겠습니다.”)

"And what about Thailand?" (“그리고 태국은?”)

"We're in the feasibility study stage." (“사업 타당성 검토 단계입니다.”)

"That's what I mean—speed it up! Contact someone for the Philippines, a broker or whoever, and set up a meeting immediately. Get everything ready so you can fly to Manila as soon as Japan is wrapped up." (“그러니까 속도를 내란 말이야! 필리핀도 브로커든 누구든 연락해서 당장 미팅 잡아. 일본 마무리되는 대로 바로 마닐라로 날아갈 수 있게 세팅하라고.”)

Jeff borrowed the exact tone Patrick had used on him an hour ago and shouted with all his might. (제프는 한 시간 전 패트릭이 자신에게 쓴 그 톤을 그대로 빌려 힘껏 고함쳤다.)

Evan was silent. (에반은 침묵했다.)

Jeff pressed his advantage and poured out the same insults he'd heard from Patrick. (제프는 기세를 몰아 패트릭에게 들었던 모욕을 그대로 쏟아부었다.)

"Evan, you're the man selling a system worth hundreds of millions of dollars. Who would trust weapons sold by someone groaning in a hospital gown? Get your head straight." (“에반, 자네는 수억 달러짜리 시스템을 파는 사람이야. 환자복 입고 골골대는 놈이 파는 무기를 누가 신뢰하겠나? 정신 똑바로 차려.”)

"I clearly understand the directives." (“지시 사항은 명확히 알겠습니다.”)

Evan cut Jeff off. (에반이 제프의 말을 잘랐다.)

"I'll report on the progress in Japan and the Philippines. That's all." (“일본과 필리핀 진행 사항은 보고하겠습니다. 그럼 이만.”)

"What? Hey, Evan—" (“뭐? 이봐, 에반——")

The call ended. (통화가 끊겼다.)

Evan set the phone on the nightstand. Not a single fingertip trembled. The sight of him picking up a glass of water with bandaged hands was so calm you'd never believe he'd just endured his superior's tirade. (에반은 폰을 협탁 위에 올려놓았다. 손끝 하나 떨리지 않았다. 붕대 감긴 손으로 물컵을 집어 드는 옆모습은, 방금 전까지 상사의 폭언을 들은 사람이라곤 믿기지 않을 만큼 평온했다.)

Watching him, Irina put down the apple she'd been peeling and let out a small chuckle. (지켜보던 이리나가 깎고 있던 사과를 내려놓으며 피식 웃었다.)

"Quite composed, aren't you. Is it okay to hang up like that?" (“꽤 의젓하네. 그렇게 해도 되는 거야?”)

Evan took a sip of water and smiled at Irina. (에반은 물을 한 모금 마시고, 이리나에게 미소를 지었다.)

"Probably not, right? But there's no logical point in getting angry at a barking dog." (“안 되겠지? 근데 짖는 개한테 논리적으로 화낼 필요는 없잖아.”)

Evan figured this wasn't the time to fight minnows. The real enemy was across the Pacific. (에반은 피라미와 싸울 때가 아니라고 생각했다. 진짜 적은 태평양 너머에 있으니까.)

Former NSC Chief of Staff in Trump's First Term: "Concerns over Coupang and Others Will Persist Until Investment in the US" (트럼프 1기 NSC 비서실장 “대미 투자 전까지는 쿠팡 등 우려 계속”)

Alexander Gray, former chief of staff of the White House National Security Council (NSC), who also served as deputy assistant to the president in the first Trump administration, predicted that "until South Korea delivers on its investment commitments to the US and there is confidence that it is making tangible contributions to American jobs and the manufacturing ecosystem, economic concerns (such as the Coupang issue) will continue to underpin the bilateral relationship." In a recent interview with this newspaper on the 3rd, Gray, who visited South Korea, cited the swift implementation of the $350 billion investment in the US agreed at last year's South Korea-US summit as the most urgent task between the two countries, and made these remarks. <<> Gray, who also served as special assistant to the White House National Economic Council (NEC) for defense industrial base issues during the first Trump administration, said, "President Trump views security and the economy as one," adding, "South Korea's implementation of the investment agreement will be a positive signal for the overall South Korea-US relationship." Gray referenced the Coupang situation and the revised Information and Communications Network Act, noting, "Numerous trends have been detected in which the South Korean government seeks to pursue legislation that discriminates against or disadvantages American companies." On why the White House and Congress are paying attention to such legislative and regulatory measures, he said, "It's not just because of Coupang alone, but rather because of a broad climate and perception that American tech companies are being discriminated against overall." <<> On the possibility of US-North Korea dialogue, Gray said, "In the remaining two years of his term after the November midterm elections, President Trump will seek opportunities to continue his efforts to conclude peace agreements around the world," adding, "It wouldn't surprise me if he tries to negotiate with North Korea again within the next two years." Noting that North Korea's troop dispatch to Russia means, unlike during his first term, the North Korea issue can no longer be separated from Russia and China, he still said, "What only President Trump and the US can do is draw North Korea into negotiations by offering the opportunity for high-level talks with the US." <<> Regarding the delay in South Korea-US consultations on securing South Korea's uranium enrichment rights, he said, "There was an aspect where the relevant personnel within the US government were focused on negotiations with Saudi Arabia," adding, "Once the Middle East crisis subsides, they can refocus on South Korea." On ways for South Korea to make tangible contributions to stability in the Strait of Hormuz, he stated, "In Washington, given the excellent capabilities of the South Korean Navy, there is an expectation that at least one or more warships will be deployed." (트럼프 1기 행정부에서 대통령 부보좌관을 겸임했던 알렉산더 그레이 전 백악관 국가안보회의(NSC) 비서실장이 “한국이 대미 투자 약속을 이행해 미국 내 일자리와 제조업 생태계에 실질적 기여를 하고 있다는 확신이 서기 전까지는, (쿠팡 문제 등) 경제적 우려 사항이 계속 양국 관계의 바탕에 깔려 있을 것”이라고 전망했다. 최근 방한한 그레이 전 비서실장은 3일 본지 인터뷰에서 지난해 한미 정상회담에서 합의한 3500억달러 대미 투자의 신속한 이행을 양국 간 가장 시급한 과제로 꼽으며 이같이 말했다.)

item.title: North Korea Calls Joint Response to 'Cyber Threats' by South Korea, US, Japan 'Defamation' (북한, 한미일 등 ‘北사이버 위협 공동대응’에 “중상모략”)
item.description:
North Korea Calls Joint Response to 'Cyber Threats' by South Korea, US, Japan 'Defamation' (북한, 한미일 등 ‘北사이버 위협 공동대응’에 “중상모략”)

North Korea has pushed back against a recent warning by 11 countries, including South Korea, the United States, and Japan, over Pyongyang's illicit foreign currency procurement through its information technology (IT) workers, calling it "groundless defamation." (북한은 최근 한국·미국·일본 등 11국이 북한의 정보통신(IT) 인력을 통한 불법적 외화 조달을 경고하고 대응을 촉구한 것에 대해 “무근거한 중상모략”이라고 반발했다.)

A spokesperson for the Foreign Ministry, in a statement released on the 4th, said that "the 'joint warning statement' spectacle that the US and its follower allies have staged by clamoring about our so-called 'cyber threats' originates from the impudent aim of tarnishing our country's image and is a routine political slander campaign," according to the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). (외무성 대변인은 4일 발표한 담화에서 “미국과 그 추종 동맹국들이 우리의 이른바 ‘사이버 위협’을 떠들며 벌려놓은 ‘공동경고문’ 발표 놀음은 우리 국가의 영상(이미지)에 먹칠을 하려는 불손한 목적에서 출발한 것으로 상투적인 정치적 비난 선동”이라고 했다고 조선중앙통신이 전했다.)

The spokesperson added that "the repeated malicious claims by member states of the 'Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team' (MSMT) are nothing more than the dissemination of untrustworthy disinformation," and that "it is the US, which monopolizes core resources in cyberspace and possesses and operates the world's largest cyber force, that is speaking nonsense by raising 'cyber threats' from other countries." (대변인은 “‘다무적제재감시팀‘(다국적 제재모니터링팀·MSMT) 성원국들의 거듭되는 악의적 주장은 신빙성이 결여된 거짓정보 유포에 불과하다”며 “사이버 공간의 핵심 자원을 독점하고 세계 최대의 사이버 전력을 보유, 운용하는 미국이 다른 나라들의 ‘사이버 위협’을 거론하는 것이야말로 어불성설”이라고 했다.)

The statement continued, "The Democratic People's Republic of Korea will thoroughly reject any attempt by the US and hostile forces to politicize and ideologize cyber issues and use them as a tool for criticism and pressure against other countries." (이어 “조선민주주의인민공화국은 사이버 문제를 정치화, 이념화하여 다른 나라에 대한 비난과 압박의 수단으로 삼으려는 미국과 적대 세력들의 그 어떤 시도도 철저히 불허할 것”이라고 했다.)

Earlier, on the 31st of last month, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the National Police Agency, together with related agencies from like-minded countries including the US, Japan, the UK, Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, and New Zealand, issued an advisory on North Korean IT workers. (앞서 외교부와 경찰청은 지난달 31일 미국, 일본, 영국, 호주, 캐나다, 프랑스, 독일, 이탈리아, 네덜란드, 뉴질랜드 등 유사 입장국 관계 기관과 함께 북한 IT 인력 관련 주의보를 발표했다.)

The participating countries stated, "North Korea relies on a network of skilled IT workers, both inside and outside the country, who assume false identities and earn income remotely to fund its illicit nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programs," and called on countries, companies, and institutions worldwide to strengthen identity verification procedures and detection of suspicious accounts, among other countermeasures. (참여국들은 “북한은 불법적 핵무기·탄도미사일 개발 자금 조달을 위해 북한 안팎에 체류하며 허위 신분을 취득하고 원격으로 수입을 벌어들이는 숙련된 IT 인력 네트워크에 의존하고 있다”며 전 세계 국가·기업·기관에 신원 확인 절차와 의심 계정 탐지를 강화하는 등 대응 조치를 시행할 것을 요구했다.)

item.title: "Democratization is an Independence Struggle"… The Resolution YS and DJ Proclaimed Simultaneously in August 1983 (“민주화는 독립 투쟁이다”… 1983년 8월 YS와 DJ가 동시에 외친 결의)
item.description:
"Democratization is an Independence Struggle"… The Resolution YS and DJ Proclaimed Simultaneously in August 1983 (“민주화는 독립 투쟁이다”… 1983년 8월 YS와 DJ가 동시에 외친 결의)

On August 13, 1983, YS wrote in his diary: "At 8:30 in the morning, I held a historic press conference at home. At the same time, Kim Dae-jung held a joint press conference in Washington." (YS는 1983년 8월 13일 일기에 적었습니다. “아침 8시 30분에 역사적인 기자회견을 집에서 했다. 같은 시간 워싱턴에서 김대중씨가 공동 기자회견을 했다.”)

Ahead of the August 15 Liberation Day, YS and DJ issued simultaneous statements in Seoul and Washington, D.C. The title was "The Struggle for Democratization Is a Struggle for the Nation's Independence and Liberation." They appealed to the people to stand firmly against the dictatorial regime together. YS later revealed in his memoirs that he personally wrote the statement. That day, YS also gave an interview to a Time magazine reporter. (8·15 광복절을 앞두고 YS와 DJ는 서울과 미국 워싱턴에서 동시에 성명을 발표했습니다. ‘민주화 투쟁은 민족의 독립과 해방을 위한 투쟁이다’라는 제목입니다. 국민과 함께 독재 권력에 결연히 맞서야 한다고 호소했습니다. 성명 문안은 YS가 직접 썼다고 훗날 회고록에서 밝혔습니다. YS는 이날 타임지(誌) 기자와 인터뷰도 진행합니다.)

YS continued to carry out activities for democracy. He also met with U.S. Congressman Stephen Solarz, chairman of the House Subcommittee on Asian and Pacific Affairs, who had come to Seoul. (YS는 민주주의를 위한 활동을 지속적으로 전개합니다. 서울에 온 미 하원 아태지구 소위원회 위원장 스티븐 솔라즈 의원과도 만났습니다.)

"I met Chairman Solarz for an hour and ten minutes. We discussed many important things. He said he had visited Gwangju and Busan. He is the first U.S. congressman to do so." (“솔라즈 위원을 1시간 10분 동안 만났다. 여러 가지로 중요한 이야기를 했다. 광주와 부산을 다녀왔다고 한다. 미국 국회의원으로서는 처음이다.”)

Earlier, on August 2, The New York Times had run an article on page two reporting on YS's 23-day hunger strike. It noted that although South Korea was undergoing economic development, it remained under the oppression of authoritarian rule, and that YS, an opposition leader who had escaped house arrest through his hunger strike, was demanding a constitutional amendment for direct presidential elections. (뉴욕타임스는 앞서 8월 2일 자 2면에 YS의 23일간 단식 투쟁을 알리는 기사를 실었습니다. 한국이 경제 발전 중이지만 권위주의 통치의 억압에 놓여 있다, 단식 투쟁으로 가택연금에서 벗어난 야권 지도자 YS는 대통령 직선제 개헌을 요구하고 있다는 내용입니다.)

That summer, temperatures soared to as high as 38 degrees Celsius. YS's struggle for democratization was also heating up. (그해 여름은 최고 섭씨 38도에 이르는 더위가 지속되었습니다. YS의 민주화 투쟁도 뜨거워지고 있었습니다.)

()

Today is an extremely hot day. (오늘은 몹시 무더운 날씨다.)

In this world, there are people who live "for money, or for honor, or for a cause." (이 세상(世上)에는 “돈 때문에 혹(惑)은 명예 때문에 또한 뜻 때문에” 세상(世上)을 사는 사람들이 있다.)

At noon, Publisher Song Seok-ho treated me to a meal. (낮에는 송석호(宋錫昊) 사장(社長)이 사식(私食)을 대접해주었다.)

In the evening, Assemblyman Hwang Myeong-su took me to the Onyang lakeside, where I enjoyed delicious eel with his wife, Comrade Ha, and others. For the first time since the hunger strike, I practiced calligraphy. (저녁에는 황명수(黃明秀) 의원(議員)이 온양 호수가에 가서 장어를 맛있게 부인(婦人)과 하(河)동지(同志) 등(等)과 같이 먹었다. 단식후(斷食後)에 처음으로 서도(書道)를 했다.)

Today is the hottest day of all. The temperature surpassed 38 degrees. (오늘이 최고(最高)로 더운 날이다. 38˚가 넘었으니 말이다.)

Last night, Chairman Jeong Byeong-hun (of Han囗 Condo) came down from Seoul, and in the morning he joined us in our room, chatting pleasantly over breakfast. For lunch, he treated us to rice and chicken stew he had made himself, which we enjoyed at the bungalow. At Chairman Jeong's invitation, I have agreed to go up to Seoul next Sunday. He is truly a kind person. (서울에서 어제 밤에 정병훈(鄭秉勳) 회장(会長)(韓囗콘도)이 내려와서 아침을 우리 방에서 함께 즐겁게 여러가지로 이야기하며 먹었다. 점심은 또한 자기(自己)가 직접 만든 밥과 닭도리탕으로 반가로(*방갈로)에서 맛있게 먹었다. 정(鄭)회장(会長)의 초청으로 내주(來週) 일요일(日曜日) 날에 상경(上京)하기로 했다. 정말 고마운 분이다.)

I visited the birthplace of Chusa. It was my second visit, but it always moves my heart. It is an unbearably hot day. (추사(秋史) 생가(生家)에 다녀왔다. 두 번째 가 보지마는 언제나 마음에 던(*든)다. 너무나도 더운 날이다.)

Another sweltering day above 38 degrees. An astonishing heat wave, the worst in 39 years. (오늘도 38˚가 넘는 무더위다. 39년째의 놀라운 더위다.)

Today, apart from going outside for an hour of morning exercise, I stayed in the hotel all day long. (오늘은 아침 운동을 위해서 한 시간(時間)동안 밖에 나갔을 뿐 하로(*루) 왼종일 Hotel 안에 있었다.)

A phone call came from Im Jeong-gyu in New York. He said that the August 2 issue of The New York Times had prominently featured an article about my press conference on page two. I can't wait to see it. (New york에서 임정규(林井圭)로부터 전화가 왔다. 8월(月) 2일(日)자 New York Times에 2면(面)에 크게 나의 회견(會見) 기사(記事)가 보도(報道)되었다고 하는 전화였다. 빨리 보구 싶구나.)

Today, I practiced calligraphy for the second time (since the hunger strike). I wrote pieces for Chairman Jeong Byeong-hun and Publisher Song Seok-ho. (오늘은 이틀째로 (단식(斷食) 후에 두번째) 서도(書道)를 했다. 정병훈(鄭秉勳) 회장(會長)과 송석호(宋錫昊) 사장(社長) 등(等)에게 글을 써 주었다.)

Hyeon-cheol went up to Seoul ahead of me regarding his matter of going to the United States. (현철(賢哲)이가 미국(美囗) 가는 문제(問題) 때문에 서울에 먼저 갔다.)

Thanks to Chairman Jeong Byeong-hun's kindness, I have decided to go to Seoul on Sunday. (정병훈(鄭秉勳) 회장(会長)의 호의(好意)로 주일(主日)날에 서울로 가기로 했다.)

Yesterday, Hyeon-cheol went to Seoul first, leaving Hye-suk alone. She said she had a good time with her friend yesterday. It had been a while since I had Korean food. (어제 현철(賢哲)이가 먼저 서울에 가고 혜숙(惠淑)이 혼자 남았다. 어제는 혜숙(惠淑)이 친구하고 재미있게 지냈다고 한다. 오랜만에 한식(韓食)을 먹어봤다.)

In the afternoon, I practiced calligraphy. I delivered the pieces to Chairman Jeong Byeong-hun and Publisher Song Seok-ho. They were overjoyed. (오후(午后)에는 서도(書道)를 했다. 정병훈(鄭秉勳) 회장(会長)과 송석호(宋錫昊) 사장(社長)에게 글을 전(傳)했다. 몹시 기쁘(*뻐)한다.)

Secretary Choi came by, and I listened to various stories from him. (최(崔) 비서(秘書)가 와서 여러가지로 이야기를 들었다.)

From Seoul, Comrade Kim Tae-ryong and the secretaries of Assemblymen Ha Je-hong and Hwang Myeong-su came to visit. (서울에서 김태룡(金泰龍) 동지(同志), 그리고 하제홍(河済泓), 황명수(黃明秀) 의원(議員)의 비서(秘書)가 다녀갔다.)

Today, I visited the tomb of Admiral Yi Sun-sin. On the way back, I stopped by Neulbom, a place run by one of our comrades, and had naengmyeon with Comrade Ha Je-hong. It was truly delicious. (오늘은 충무공(忠武公) 묘소에 가봤다. 그길로 늘봄이란 우리 동지(同志)가 하는 늘봄에 가서 하제홍(河済泓) 동지(同志)와 함께 냉면을 먹었다. 정말 맛있다.)

Today, I wrote more calligraphy than ever before—fourteen pieces. I wrote them with the names of our comrades in Onyang. (오늘은 붓글씨를 제일(第一) 많이 썼다. 14장을 써서(*썼으)니 말이다. 온양(溫陽)의 동지(同志)들의 이름을 넣어 썼다.)

While having dinner, I ran into Kwon Oh-hyeon, the publisher of the Busan Ilbo and a fellow alumnus of mine. (저녁을 먹다가 권오(權五)현 부산일보(釜山日報) 사장(社長) 나의 동창(同窓)을 맞(*만)났다.)

Today is Sunday. (오늘은 주일(主日)이다.)

I attended worship service at the Dogo Hot Springs Church. Pastor Kim Deok-hwa presides there. He introduced me publicly. It was bolder than Chunghyeon Church. (도고온천(道高溫泉) 교회(敎會)에서 예배를 봤다. 김덕화 목사(牧師)가 시무한다. 나를 공개적(公開的)으로 소개(紹介)를 한다. 충현교회(敎會)보다 대담하다.)

Amid a send-off from Publisher Song Seok-ho and all the executives, I departed Dogo. Even though it was only a week, I feel a sense of emptiness now that I have left the Dogo Hotel life behind. (송석호(宋錫昊) 사장(社長) 이하 간부(幹部) 전원(全員)이 전송하는 가운데 도고(道高)를 떠나왔다. 도고(道高)Hotel 생활(生活)에서 벗으(*어)나니까 일주일간(一週日間)이지 마는 허전하다.)

No sooner had I arrived in Seoul than this government startled the people again. It issued an air-raid warning—not a security alert. A Chinese MiG-21 had defected. I can only sigh at how much they will make of this and use it for propaganda. (서울데 도착하자마자 이 정부(政府)에서 또 국민(囗民)을 놀라게 한다. 공습 공(*경)보를 발(發)한 것이다. 경비 공보가 아니라 말이다. 중공(中共)의 미그21기(機)가 귀순해 온 것이다. 또 이것을 가지고 얼마나 떠들고 선전을 하겠는지 정말 답답하다.)

Today is another quite hot day. (오늘도 상당(相當)히 무더운 날이다.)

Vice President Lee Min-woo and many others came to visit. (이민우(李敏雨) 부총재(副總裁)와 그 외(外)에 많은 분들이 다녀갔다.)

From Japan, Chairman Kim Seok-won came with a Japanese man. (일본(日本)에서 김석원(金錫沅) 사장(社長)과 일본인(日本人) 한 사람이 같이 왔다.)

Word came from U.S. Congressman Solarz, suggesting we meet at the Chosun Hotel tomorrow at 4:30. (미국(美囗)의 Solarz 의원(議員)이 내일(來日) 4시(時)30분(分)에 조선Hotel에서 맞(*만)나자고 연락이 왔다.)

Many people came by in the morning. (아침에 많은 분들 다녀갔다.)

At noon, since we had gone to Dogo and back, Mi-ae and I went to "Marado" and truly enjoyed a delicious Japanese meal. (낮에는 우리들이 도고(道高)에 갔다 오고 해서 미애와 “마라도”에 가서 정말 맛있게 화식(和食)을 먹었다.)

From Los Angeles, Chairman Cha Sang-Lull, the brother of Director Cha of the bureau, came by and left. (미국(美囗) Los에서 차(車)국장(局長) 동생인 차상(車相)Lull 사장(社長)이 왔다가 갔다.)

At 4:30 in the afternoon, I met for an hour and ten minutes with Congressman Solarz, chairman of the U.S. House Subcommittee on Asian and Pacific Affairs. We discussed many important matters. He said he had visited Gwangju and Busan. He is the first U.S. congressman to do so. (오후(午后)에 4시(時)30분(分) 미국(美囗) 하원(下院)의 아태평양(亞太平洋) 지구(地區) 소위원회(小委員會) 위원장(委員長)인 Solarz 의원(議員)을 1시간(時間)10분(分)동안 맞(*만)났다. 여러가지로 중요(重要)한 이야기를 했다. 광주(光州)와 부산(釜山)을 다녀왔다고 한다. 미국(美囗) 국회의원(國會議員)으로써(*서)는 처음이다.)

I also had a message delivered to Reverend Mun Ik-hwan. (문익환(文益煥) 목사(牧師)님에게도 전(傳)달을 했다.)

From New York, Mr. Kim brought a copy of The New York Times from August 2 containing the article on my press conference. It takes up the entire second page. (New York에서 Mr Kim New York Times의 8월(月)2일(日)자(字)의 나의 회견기사(會見記事)가 있는 신문(新聞)을 가지고 왔다. 2면(面)에 전면(全面)이다.)

At noon, I had lunch with Mr. Kim Byeong-tae and Attorney Oh. (낮에는 김병태(金炳泰)씨(氏)와 오(吳)변호사와 같이 점심을 먹었다.)

Afterward, it was said that a police officer asked to see Mr. Kim Byeong-tae's ID. What an absurd thing. (그 후(后)에 김병태(金炳泰)씨(氏)의 신분증(证)을 보자고 경찰관(警察官)이 봤다고 한다. 정말 어처구니 없는 일이다.)

After a long time, Assemblymen Hwang Nak-ju and Kim Dong-yeong came by, and we talked and discussed plans to attend the unveiling ceremony of Inchon's statue in Gochang on the 15th. (오랜만에 황낙주(黃珞周), 김동영(金東英) 의원(議員) 등(等)이 와서 이야기를 나누며 15일(日)에 고(高)창에 인촌(仁村)의 동상 제막식(式)에 갈 상의(相議)를 했다.)

At noon, I had lunch with Vice President Park Yeong-rok and discussed future matters. (낮에는 박영록(朴永錄) 부총재(副總裁)와 점심을 먹으며 앞으로 문제(問題)를 의논했다.)

In the afternoon, Assemblyman Han Yeong-su came and stayed for a long conversation. (오후(午后)에 한영수(韓英洙) 의원(議員)이 와서 장시간(長時間) 이야기를 하고 갔다.)

Today, I stayed home all day. In the evening, the weather turned very bad, with thunder and heavy rain pouring down. (오늘은 하로(*루) 종일 집에 있었다. 날씨 저녁 때에 몹시 나빠지며 뇌성과 비가 몹시 나(*내)렸다.)

This morning, the weather is very clear. At 8:30 in the morning, I held a historic press conference at home. At the same hour, Kim Dae-jung held a joint press conference in Washington. Im Jeong-gyu and Dr. Jo Hong-gyu called from the United States. That was 6:30 p.m. on the 12th by U.S. time—that is, 8:30 a.m. on the 13th by Korean time. I don't know about other places yet, but the Japanese newspapers are running it as the top story on the front page. (오늘 아침에는 몹시 맑은 날씨다. 아침 8시(時)30분(分)에 역사적(歷史的)인 기자회견(記者會見)을 집에 했다. 같은 시간(時間)인 와신톤(*워싱턴)에 김대중(金大中)씨(氏)가 공동(共同) 기자회견(記者會見)을 했다. 미국(美囗)에서 임정규(林井圭)와 조(趙)홍규 박사(博士)가 전화를 해왔다. 김대중(金大中)씨(氏)가 미국(美囗) 시간(時間)으로 12일(日) 저녁 6시(時)30분(分) 다시 말하면 한국시간(韓囗時間)으로 13일 아침 8시(時) 30분(分)이다. 딴데는 아직 모르겠고 일본신문(日本新聞)들은 일면(一面) 톱이라고 한다.)

In the afternoon, I met with Time magazine correspondent Mr. Chang. (오후에 Time 잡지 기자(記者) Mr 장과 회견(會見)을 했다.)

item.title: 'Ist Corps That Mistook US Drone' Now Mistook Friendly Aircraft for Enemy? (‘美무인기 오인’ 1군단, 이번엔 아군기를 적군기로 오인?”)
item.description:
'Ist Corps That Mistook US Drone' Now Mistook Friendly Aircraft for Enemy? (‘美무인기 오인’ 1군단, 이번엔 아군기를 적군기로 오인?”)

Claims have emerged that the Army's 1st Corps, which recently nearly intercepted a US reconnaissance drone after mistaking it for an unidentified flying object, has now mistaken a friendly aircraft for an enemy one, going so far as to initiate procedures for issuing the 'Durumi' air-defense readiness alert. (최근 미군의 정찰용 무인기를 미확인 비행체로 오인해 요격할 뻔했던 육군 1군단이 아군기를 적군기로 오인해 대공 준비 태세인 ‘두루미’ 발령 절차까지 밟는 일이 벌어졌다는 주장이 나왔다.)

People Power Party lawmaker Seong Il-jong held a press conference at the National Assembly in Yeouido, Seoul, on the 4th and stated, "Another major incident occurred yesterday at the Army's 1st Corps," adding, "This time, it wasn't even the US military—they mistook a friendly drone for an enemy one, coming right up to the point of shooting it down and just before issuing the 'Durumi' alert." (국민의힘 성일종 의원은 4일 서울 여의도 국회에서 기자회견을 열고 “육군 1군단에서 어제 또다시 초대형 사고가 터졌다”며 “이번에는 미군도 아니고 아군 무인기를 적군으로 오인해 격추 직전까지 가고, ‘두루미’ 발령 직전까지 갔었다”고 밝혔다.)

According to Seong's account, on the 3rd, the Army Test and Evaluation Group notified the 1st Corps of its plan to conduct flights for drone test evaluations. The drone flight then proceeded normally over 1st Corps airspace. (성 의원의 말을 종합하면, 3일 육군 시험평가단은 ‘드론 시험 평가를 위한 비행을 실시하겠다’는 계획을 1군단 측에 통보했다. 그리고 드론 비행이 1군단 상공에서 정상적으로 이뤄졌다.)

The problem arose that afternoon. When another drone test evaluation took place over 1st Corps airspace around 4:20 p.m., the 1st Corps reportedly mistook it for an enemy aircraft. Seong said, "They reportedly even went through the procedures to issue the 'Durumi' air-defense readiness alert," adding, "If they couldn't distinguish between an enemy aircraft and a friendly drone during the afternoon flight, doesn't that mean our military's operational system has completely collapsed?" (문제는 이날 오후 발생했다. 오후 4시 20분쯤 또다시 1군단 상공에서 드론 시험 평가가 이뤄지자 1군단은 이것을 적군기로 오인했다고 한다. 성 의원은 “대공 준비 태세인 ‘두루미’를 발령하기 위한 절차까지 밟았었다고 한다”며 “오후 비행에서 적기인지 아군 드론인지 구별도 못 했다면 우리 군의 작전 시스템이 완전히 붕괴된 것 아니냐”고 했다.)

Previously, on the 30th of last month, a subordinate unit of the Army's 1st Corps had mistaken a US reconnaissance drone, deployed as part of a ROK-US joint exercise, for an 'unidentified flying object' and nearly intercepted it. It was revealed that a 1st Corps staff member had received advance notice of the drone flight plan from the US military but failed to report it up the chain of command. (앞서 육군 1군단에서는 지난달 30일 한미 연합 훈련의 일환으로 출격한 미군의 정찰용 무인기를 예하 부대가 ‘미확인 비행체’로 오인해 요격할 뻔한 일도 있었다. 1군단 실무자가 미군으로부터 무인기 비행 계획을 사전에 통보받고도 상부에 보고하지 않아 발생한 일로 드러났다.)

Seong said, "At this rate, if war breaks out, can our military properly identify friendly forces and our own citizens?" adding, "If war comes, will they mistake our citizens for enemy troops and shoot them?" (성 의원은 “이래서야 전쟁 나면 우리 군이 아군과 우리 국민은 제대로 식별할 수 있겠느냐”며 “전쟁이 나면 우리 국민도 적군으로 오인해서 사살할 것이냐”고 했다.)

He then held Defense Minister Ahn Kyu-baek responsible. Seong stated, "Minister Ahn, in particular, is the one who has left our military in a state of uncontrollable chaos," and called for his "immediate resignation." He continued, "The collapse of the military's coordination system and command structure is entirely the responsibility of its superiors. If they don't feel responsibility even after our military has crumbled this miserably, they have no qualification whatsoever to hold public office. An immediate resignation is the only way to take responsibility." (그러면서 안규백 국방 장관에게 책임을 물었다. 성 의원은 “특히 안 장관은 우리 군을 통제 불능 상태로 만든 장본인”이라며 “즉각 사퇴하라”고 했다. 이어 “군의 협조 체계와 통제 시스템이 붕괴된 것은 모두 상관의 책임”이라며 “이렇게까지 우리 군이 처참하게 무너졌는데도 책임감을 느끼지 못한다면 공직을 맡을 자격이 전혀 없는 것이다. 오로지 즉각 사퇴만이 책임질 수 있는 유일한 방법”이라고 했다.)

item.title: Jung Cheong-rae targets Kim Min-seok: "If Shincheonji can't reveal the evidence, apologize first" (정청래, 김민석 겨냥 “신천지 근거 못 밝힐 거면 사과부터 하라”)
item.description:
Jung Cheong-rae targets Kim Min-seok: "If Shincheonji can't reveal the evidence, apologize first" (정청래, 김민석 겨냥 “신천지 근거 못 밝힐 거면 사과부터 하라”)

Jung Cheong-rae, who is running for Democratic Party leadership, targeted candidate Kim Min-seok on the 4th, saying, "If you can't clarify the basis for the Shincheonji allegations, then apologize first." (더불어민주당 당대표 선거에 출마한 정청래 후보는 4일 김민석 후보를 겨냥해 “신천지 의혹 제기 근거를 못 밝힐 거면 일단 사과부터 하라”고 했다.)

On Facebook that day, candidate Jeong said, "How long will you keep pushing the party to the brink and denying me?" and added, "Stop irresponsibly shutting your mouth—apologize immediately." (정 후보는 이날 페이스북에서 “언제까지 당을 사지로 몰아넣고 나 몰라라 할 것인가”라며 “무책임하게 ‘입꾹닫’하지 말고 당장 사과부터 하라”고 했다.)

In a notice that day, Jeong's camp stated, "We inform you that we have taken legal action against media outlets and YouTube channels that reported or spread false information with the intent to influence the party's primary in relation to a specific religion or individual, on charges of publishing false information, stating false information, defamation, and false accusations." (정 후보 측은 이날 공지에서 “특정 종교, 특정 인물과 관련해 당내 경선에 영향을 끼칠 목적으로 허위사실을 보도 또는 유포한 언론, 유튜브 등에 대해 허위사실 공표, 허위사실 적시 명예훼손, 무고 등의 혐의로 법적 조치했음을 알린다”고 했다.)

Jung's camp stated, "Jung's claims about the anti-Myeong tripartite secret alliance are clearly the basis of the act, and we have already stated several times that an immediate investigation and severe disciplinary action should be imposed if there is no evidence." (정 후보 측은 “정 후보는 반명-분열주의-신천지 3자 비밀연합 주장이 명백한 해당 행위이며, 이에 대해 즉시 조사해서 근거가 없다면 중징계해야 함을 이미 수차례 밝힌 바 있다”고 했다.)

Candidate Jeong also said on this day, "The organization cannot overcome the wind," and added, "Just as Roh Moo-hyun's wish defeated Lee In-je's organization, please let Jeong Cheong-rae's wish defeat Kim Min-seok's organization." (정 후보는 또 이날 “조직은 바람을 이길 수 없다”며 “노무현의 바람이 이인제의 조직을 이겼듯이 정청래의 바람이 김민석의 조직을 이기게 해달라”고도 했다.)

item.title: Lee calls abolishing prosecutorial investigative powers "an inevitable measure for justice"... Unlikely to exercise veto power (李, 검찰 수사권 폐지에 “사필귀정의 필연적 조치”...거부권 행사 안할 듯)
item.description:
Lee calls abolishing prosecutorial investigative powers "an inevitable measure for justice"... Unlikely to exercise veto power (李, 검찰 수사권 폐지에 “사필귀정의 필연적 조치”...거부권 행사 안할 듯)

()

On the 4th, President Lee Jae-myung commented on the Democratic Party's forced passage of the amendment to the Criminal Procedure Act on the 31st of last month to completely abolish the prosecution's direct investigative power, saying, "The separation of investigation and prosecution is the first step toward normalizing the abnormal criminal justice system," and added, "It is an inevitable measure to keep all power institutions under the control of the people without exception." (이재명 대통령은 4일 더불어민주당이 지난달 31일 검찰의 직접 수사권을 전면 폐지하는 형사소송법 개정안을 강행 처리한 데 대해 “수사·기소 분리는 비정상적 형사 사법 시스템을 정상화하는 첫 출발”이라며 “모든 권력 기관은 예외 없이 국민의 통제 아래 두겠다는 사필귀정의 필연적 조치”라고 했다.)

President Lee commented on the amendment to the Criminal Procedure Act, noting that concerns are mounting in the legal and academic circles that 'crime victims will be isolated and criminals will benefit,' and that the opposition is demanding the president's 'right to request reconsideration (veto) in the National Assembly,' saying, "There is much controversy and disagreement," but added, "It is difficult to see it as a situation serious enough to deny the legislative power of the National Assembly." This effectively refused to exercise the veto. (이 대통령은 형소법 개정안 내용을 두고 법조계와 학계 등에서 ‘범죄 피해자는 고립되고 범죄자는 이득을 볼 것’이라는 우려가 쏟아지고, 야당에서는 대통령의 ‘국회 재의 요구권(거부권)’ 행사를 요구하는 상황에 대해 “많은 논란과 이견이 있다”면서도 “국회 입법권을 부정할 만큼 심각한 상황이라고 보기 어렵다”고 말했다. 거부권 행사를 사실상 거부한 것이다.)

In his remarks at the Cabinet meeting that day, President Lee said, "Exercising veto power does not mean there are differing opinions, but according to the principle of separation of powers, the exercise of authority by the other party itself violates the separation of powers, and only if it violates constitutional order can the other party's authority be denied. This is the view of constitutional scholars." President Lee reiterated, "It is truly difficult to say that the current situation has reached the point of denying legislative authority." (이 대통령은 이날 국무회의 모두 발언에서 “거부권 행사라고 하는 것이 의견이 다르다고 할 수 있는 것이 아니고 삼권분립 원칙에 따라서 상대의 권한 행사 자체가 삼권분립에 위배된다, 헌정 질서에 위반된다고 해야 상대의 권능을 부정할 수 있다는 게 어쨌든 헌법학계의 의견”이라며 이같이 말했다. 이 대통령은 “지금 상태로는 입법권을 부정할 정도에 이른다고 보기가 참 어렵다”고 재차 언급했다.)

President Lee also commented that the complete abolition of the prosecution's direct investigative authority is justified. President Lee said, "Over the past several decades, the prosecution has exercised extremely excessive and concentrated authority across the entire criminal justice system, from investigations to indictments and warrant requests," and added, "Under this abnormal criminal justice system, certain groups within the prosecution have freely abused this authority to conduct investigations for the purpose of prosecution, covering up existing cases or designating individuals as investigation targets to punish them through separate investigations, We have repeatedly conducted dust-dusting investigations as if it were a routine practice." (이 대통령은 검찰의 직접 수사권 전면 폐지가 정당하다는 취지의 언급도 했다. 이 대통령은 “지난 수십 년 동안 검찰은 수사부터 기소, 영장 청구 등 형사 사법 체계 전반에 걸쳐 매우 과대하고 집중된 권한을 행사해 왔다”며 “이 같은 비정상적 형사 사법 시스템하에서 검찰 내 일부 집단은 기소를 위해서 수사를 할 수 있다는 이 권한을 무소불위로 악용하며 있는 사건을 덮거나, (수사 대상으로) 누군가를 정해 놓고 처벌하기 위해 별건 수사, 먼지떨이 수사를 관행처럼 되풀이해 왔다”고 했다.)

He continued, "In that process, innocent citizens suffered harm that was hard to bear, and it was common for them to sacrifice their own lives," and added, "Moreover, the majority of prosecutors who quietly and faithfully performed their duties had to bear the stigma of being political prosecutors." (이어 “그 과정에서 무고한 국민이 감내하기 어려운 피해를 입었고 심지어 스스로 삶을 저버리는 일도 자주 발생했다”며 “또한 묵묵히 자신의 직무를 충실히 수행한 대다수 검사들까지 정치 검찰이라는 오명을 뒤집어써야 했다”고 했다.)

However, President Lee said that the side effects of the complete abolition of prosecutorial investigative powers must be actively addressed. President Lee said, "There is no reform in the world that can be easily concluded with a single institutional change," and added, "From the public's perspective, I will carefully inspect whether the system changed to its original intent is functioning properly, and if there are any shortcomings or errors, I will promptly, decisively, and thoroughly supplement them." (하지만 이 대통령은 검찰 수사권 전면 폐지에 따른 부작용은 적극 보완해야 한다고 했다. 이 대통령은 “한 번의 제도 변경으로 쉽게 종결되는 그런 개혁은 세상 어디에도 없다”며 “국민의 눈높이에서 원래 취지대로 변경된 시스템이 제대로 작동하는지 세심하게 점검하고 부족하거나 잘못된 부분이 있다면 신속하고 과감하게 그리고 철저히 보완하도록 하겠다”고 했다.)

President Lee has repeatedly stated that some supplementary investigative powers should be retained by the prosecution, but when hardliners within the ruling party strongly demanded 'complete abolition,' he changed his stance, saying, 'I will leave it to the National Assembly's judgment.' Within the ruling party, there is an interpretation that this is a shift in stance with the mindset of hardliners and hardline supporters ahead of the party convention. He said he changed his stance to prevent Democratic Party members from 'defecting' toward the president. (이 대통령은 그동안 검찰의 보완 수사권은 일부 남겨둬야 한다는 입장을 수차례 밝혔지만, 여당 내 강경파가 ‘전면 폐지’를 강하게 주장하자 ‘국회 판단에 맡기겠다’고 입장을 바꿨다. 여권 내에서는 “당 전당대회를 앞두고 강경파와 강성 지지층을 의식한 입장 변화”라는 해석이 나왔다. 대통령을 향한 민주당 권리당원의 ‘이탈’을 막기 위해 입장을 바꿨다는 것이다.)

Although the prosecution can no longer conduct direct investigations, President Lee said, "Even if the name and role change, the prosecution's duty to protect the people and the rule of law does not become any lighter," and added, "As a representative of the public interest, the prosecution will fulfill its responsibilities as a human rights defender more faithfully and become a prosecution for all citizens." (검찰이 이제 직접 수사를 못 하게 됐지만, 이 대통령은 “이름과 역할은 변해도 국민과 법치를 수호하는 검찰의 책무는 조금 더 가벼워지지 않는다”며 “검찰은 대표적인 공익의 대표자인 만큼 인권 수호자로서의 책임을 보다 충실히 수행해 국민 모두의 검찰로 거듭나기 바란다”고 했다.)

Regarding concerns about police undermining due to the complete abolition of prosecutorial investigative powers, President Lee said, "I hope the police will also become a trustworthy police force for the people by dedicating themselves to eradicating internal corruption, providing practical protection for victims, and strengthening democratic control, with a determined attitude." (검찰 수사권 전면 폐지로 ‘경찰 비대화’ 우려가 나오는 데 대해, 이 대통령은 “경찰 역시 뼈를 깎는 자세로 내부 비리 근절과 피해자의 실질적 보호, 민주적 통제 강화에 총력 매진함으로써 믿음직한 국민의 경찰로 거듭나기 바란다”고 했다.)

item.title: Opposition Says "Lee's Tax Bomb Declaration, a Repeat of the Moon Administration's Disaster" (野 “李 세금폭탄 투하선언, 文정권 참사반복”)
item.description:
Opposition Says "Lee's Tax Bomb Declaration, a Repeat of the Moon Administration's Disaster" (野 “李 세금폭탄 투하선언, 文정권 참사반복”)

The People Power Party launched a fierce offensive against the "2026 Tax Reform Plan," whose core is tax hikes targeting high-priced homes and non-resident single-homeowners, calling it a "declaration of a tax bomb." Regarding this tax reform plan, a self-deprecating phrase is circulating online: "If you buy, acquisition tax; if you sell, capital gains tax; if you live, comprehensive real estate tax; if you own, holding tax; if you give, gift tax; if you die, inheritance tax; if you don't buy, jeonse and monthly rent; and apartment prices keep soaring." <<> Chung Jin-suk, the People Power Party's floor leader, said on Facebook on the 4th, "This is the worst simultaneous tax hike that even ignores the OECD's recommendation to lower transaction taxes when raising holding taxes." Regarding the sharp increases in comprehensive real estate tax and capital gains tax targeting high-priced homes and non-resident single-homeowners, Chung said, "This is effectively punitive taxation," adding, "The burden will ultimately be passed on to jeonse and monthly rent prices, causing them to skyrocket and spreading the burden to ordinary people." <<> President Lee Jae-myung's remarks during last year's presidential campaign, when he said "I will not try to control housing prices through taxes," also came under fire. Floor leader Chung said, "With this, all the promises of 'candidate Lee Jae-myung' have collapsed," adding, "President Lee Jae-myung's real estate policy, which chose a tax bomb, is running in completely the opposite direction from his promises." He continued, "President Lee deceived the people during the election," and "Even President Moon Jae-in did not make a 180-degree reversal to the point of breaking his pledges like this." <<> Secretary-General Chung Hee-yong also said, "This tax reform plan even targets benefits needed by ordinary people and the youth, such as the marriage and childbirth tax credit, electric vehicle tax support, and additional public transportation deductions," adding, "It's as if even the minimal tax safety net for ordinary people and future generations has been stripped away." <<> Lawmakers from the capital region also raised their voices in unison against the tax reform plan. Lawmaker Na Kyung-won (Seoul Dongjak-gu) said, "The Lee Jae-myung administration and the Democratic Party are determined to repeat the real estate disaster of the Moon Jae-in administration, which tried to control housing prices with taxes as a weapon and divided the people into 'the haves and the have-nots,'" adding, "The president may have avoided the tax bomb by selling his home knowing the tax reform plans in advance, but powerless citizens have nowhere to escape." <<> Lawmaker Ahn Cheol-soo (Gyeonggi Bundang-gap) said, "Real estate taxes are a problem, but in the securities sector, they've hidden poison clauses that plunder the accounts of retail investors," adding, "They preach about advancing the capital market, yet they're pushing the entire nation into a mindless domestic stock market." Lawmaker Kim Yong-tae (Gyeonggi Pocheon·Gapyeong) also warned, "Public sentiment in Seongnam regarding real estate will turn into anger toward the government and ruling party." <<> There were also reactions to the real estate transaction tax hike such as "Are they telling ordinary people to just go and die?" As the phrase circulated across online communities—"If you buy, acquisition tax; if you sell, capital gains tax; if you live, comprehensive real estate tax; if you own, holding tax; if you give, gift tax; if you die, inheritance tax; if you don't buy, jeonse and monthly rent; and apartment prices keep soaring"—Supreme Council member Shin Dong-wook said, "This is the public sentiment out there." He added, "People like President Lee Jae-myung, who have power, can freely set up mortgages and properly use private lending, will survive somehow," and "It's essentially telling the powerless and penniless ordinary people to go and die." (국민의힘은 고가(高價) 주택·비거주 1주택자를 겨냥한 증세가 골자인 ‘2026 세제 개편안’에 대해 “세금 폭탄 투하 선언”이라면서 파상공세했다. 이번 세제 개편안을 두고 온라인 공간에서는 ‘사자니 취득세, 팔자니 양도세, 살자니 종부세, 있자니 보유세, 주자니 증여세, 죽자니 상속세, 안 사자니 전월세, 아파트값 급등세’라는 자조 섞인 얘기도 회자되고 있다.)

item.title: President Lee: "A Worker Earning 1 Billion Won Pays 50% in Taxes, but Someone Earning 10 Billion Won from Real Estate Pays Only a Few Hundred Million?" (李대통령 “10억 번 근로자는 세금 50% 내는데, 100억 부동산 버는 사람이 몇 억 내서야”)
item.description:
President Lee: "A Worker Earning 1 Billion Won Pays 50% in Taxes, but Someone Earning 10 Billion Won from Real Estate Pays Only a Few Hundred Million?" (李대통령 “10억 번 근로자는 세금 50% 내는데, 100억 부동산 버는 사람이 몇 억 내서야”)

President Lee Jae-myung emphasized that regarding the real estate tax reform, the measure on the suspension of heavy capital gains taxes for multi-homeowners is "not a complete abolition of heavy taxation, but a differential heavy taxation based on the timing of disposal." He pointed out the severe inequity between earned income tax and real estate capital gains tax and announced a major overhaul of the tax system. <<> ◇"Extension of the Exit Route for Multi-Homeowners? Completely Different from Before" <<> In response to criticism that he had announced in May this year that "there will be no further extension of the heavy tax suspension for multi-homeowners," only to give them another opportunity, the president said at a Cabinet meeting on the 4th that "this is not true." He was referring to the part of the tax reform plan announced the previous day concerning the suspension of heavy capital gains taxes for multi-homeowners. He added, "When we discussed the policy back then, I said we must never make people feel like 'I sold too early.' This measure does not completely abolish heavy taxation but opens an exit route over one to two years, applying heavy taxation differentially." <<> Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Economy and Finance Koo Yun-cheol, who gave the briefing, explained, "Originally, the heavy tax surcharge is 20 percentage points for two-homeowners and 30 percentage points for three-homeowners, but under this plan, if disposal occurs within one year, only 5 percentage points for two-homeowners and 10 percentage points for three-homeowners are applied; if disposed of within two years, 10 percentage points and 20 percentage points respectively are applied, and after that, it reverts to the original rates." <<> The president said, "Please make sure to explain the policy to the public without causing misunderstandings. Decisions should be made carefully, but once made, they should be implemented firmly without flip-flopping, so that the government's policies gain credibility." <<> ◇"A Worker Earning 1 Billion Won Pays 50% in Taxes... It's Unfair That Real Estate Speculation Income Isn't Taxed" <<> While checking the highest income tax bracket for earned income, the president received a report from Policy Chief Kim Yong-beom that "the highest tax rate for taxable income exceeding 1 billion won annually is 45%, and including local income tax, it applies up to 49.5%." The president then said, "For income exceeding 1 billion won, workers diligently work and pay about half of their income in taxes. But now, in real estate, even if capital gains reach the 1 billion won level (in Korean units, 10 billion won), due to various deductions, the actual tax paid amounts to only a few hundred million won—isn't that the current structure?" (Note: The original Korean uses '100억' meaning 10 billion won, and '몇 억' meaning a few hundred million won.) <<> He added, "If the value of one's primary residence rises by chance, it's right to give a discount, but if someone buys property for investment or speculation and earns tens of billions of won while paying almost no tax, that is extremely inequitable compared to workers' earned income. It doesn't align with the purpose of housing protection and, on the contrary, ends up protecting real estate investment and speculation." <<> ◇"Without Tax Normalization, Equity Will Be Destroyed" <<> The president said, "Tax matters are difficult and unpopular from the government's standpoint, but if the tax system is not normalized, serious equity problems will arise. During the legislative notice period for tax policy, if there are any unfair or clearly flawed parts in the process of gathering public opinion, we will readily correct them, so please share your views extensively." (이재명 대통령이 부동산 세제 개편 중 다주택자 양도소득세 중과 유예 조치와 관련해 “완전한 중과 폐지가 아닌 처분 시기에 따른 차등 중과 방식”이라고 강조했다. 근로소득세와 부동산 양도소득세 간의 심각한 불형평성을 지적하며 대대적인 조세 정비도 예고했다.)

item.title: Criminal Procedure Act Amendment Fully Abolishing Prosecutors' Investigation Powers Passes Cabinet Meeting (‘검찰 수사권 전면폐지’ 형사소송법 개정안, 국무회의 통과)
item.description:
Criminal Procedure Act Amendment Fully Abolishing Prosecutors' Investigation Powers Passes Cabinet Meeting (‘검찰 수사권 전면폐지’ 형사소송법 개정안, 국무회의 통과)

The amendment to the Criminal Procedure Act that fully abolishes prosecutors' direct investigation powers was passed at a Cabinet meeting on the 4th. President Lee Jae-myung presided over the Cabinet meeting at the presidential office (Cheong Wa Dae) that day and approved the Criminal Procedure Act amendment that was on the agenda for deliberation. (검찰의 직접 수사권을 전면 폐지하는 형사소송법 개정안이 4일 국무회의에서 통과됐다. 이재명 대통령은 이날 청와대에서 국무회의를 주재하면서, 심의 안건으로 올라온 형소법 개정안을 의결했다.)

The passed Criminal Procedure Act removes the legal basis for prosecutors' direct investigation powers and supplementary investigation powers over cases referred by the police. This marks the elimination of provisions that had been maintained for 72 years since the enactment of the Criminal Procedure Act in 1954. (통과된 형소법은 검사의 직접 수사권, 경찰에서 송치된 사건에 대한 보완 수사권의 법적 근거를 삭제했다. 1954년 형소법 제정 이후 72년 동안 유지된 내용이 이번에 사라진 것이다.)

New provisions have been included allowing courts to issue dismissal of prosecution rulings on grounds such as serious illegal investigations or a marked deviation from prosecutorial discretion. The opposition parties are criticizing this as an attempt to nullify President Lee's trials through dismissal of prosecution rulings. (법원이 중대한 위법 수사, 소추 재량권의 현저한 일탈 등의 사유로 공소 기각 판결을 할 수 있도록 하는 내용은 새로 포함됐다. 야당에서는 이 대통령의 재판을 ‘공소 기각’으로 없애려는 목적이라고 비판하고 있다.)

In his opening remarks at the meeting that day, President Lee said of the Criminal Procedure Act amendment, "Separating investigation and prosecution is the first step toward normalizing an abnormal criminal justice system," adding, "It is an inevitable measure of justice prevailing in the end to place all power institutions under the control of the people without exception." President Lee had repeatedly expressed concerns about fully abolishing prosecutors' supplementary investigation powers, but as debate intensified within the ruling party, he changed his position to "leave it to the National Assembly's judgment." (이 대통령은 이날 회의 모두 발언에서 형소법 개정안에 대해 “수사·기소 분리는 비정상적 형사 사법 시스템을 정상화하는 첫 출발”이라며 “모든 권력 기관은 예외 없이 국민의 통제 아래 두겠다는 사필귀정의 필연적 조치”라고 했다. 이 대통령은 검찰의 보완 수사권을 전면 폐지하는 데 대한 우려 입장을 수차례 밝혔지만, 여당 내에서 논쟁이 가열되자 ‘국회 판단에 맡기겠다’고 입장을 바꿨다.)

Prior to the Cabinet meeting that day, opposition parties including the People Power Party demanded that President Lee exercise his power to request reconsideration (veto power), but President Lee did not exercise the veto. Regarding the veto demands, President Lee said, "It is difficult to see this as a situation serious enough to deny the National Assembly's legislative authority." He added, "According to constitutional scholars, exercising the veto is not simply a matter of differing opinions; under the principle of separation of powers, you can only deny the other branch's authority if the exercise of that authority itself violates the separation of powers or the constitutional order. In the current situation, it is very difficult to see that the legislative power has been denied to that extent." (이날 국무회의에 앞서 국민의힘 등 야당에서는 이 대통령의 재의 요구권(거부권) 행사를 요구했지만, 이 대통령은 거부권을 행사하지 않았다. 이 대통령은 거부권 요구에 대해 “국회 입법권을 부정할 만큼 심각한 상황이라고 보기 어렵다“고 했다. 이 대통령은 ”거부권 행사라고 하는 것이 의견이 다르다고 할 수 있는 것이 아니고 삼권분립 원칙에 따라서 상대의 권한 행사 자체가 삼권분립에 위배된다, 헌정 질서에 위반된다고 해야 상대의 권능을 부정할 수 있다는 게 어쨌든 헌법학계의 의견“이라며 ”지금 상태로는 입법권을 부정할 정도에 이른다고 보기가 참 어렵다”고 했다.)

President Lee left open the possibility of further amendments to the Criminal Procedure Act. Regarding concerns about side effects such as an "overpowered police" arising from the concentration of investigation powers in the police following implementation of the amendment, President Lee said, "We will carefully monitor whether the changed system operates properly and promptly, boldly, and thoroughly address any shortcomings or errors." (이 대통령은 형소법 추가 개정 가능성은 열어뒀다. 형소법 개정안 시행으로 경찰에 수사권이 집중되며 우려되는 ‘경찰 비대화’ 등 부작용에 대해, 이 대통령은 “변경된 시스템이 제대로 작동하는지 세심하게 점검하고 부족하거나 잘못된 부분이 있다면 신속하고 과감하게 그리고 철저히 보완하도록 하겠다”고 했다.)

item.title: People Power Party: "Abolishing Supplementary Investigation Rights Leaves Only the Powerless Victims Wronged... President Lee Must Exercise Veto" (국민의힘 “보완수사권 폐지, 힘없는 피해자만 억울...李대통령 거부권 행사해야")
item.description:
People Power Party: "Abolishing Supplementary Investigation Rights Leaves Only the Powerless Victims Wronged... President Lee Must Exercise Veto" (국민의힘 “보완수사권 폐지, 힘없는 피해자만 억울...李대통령 거부권 행사해야")

The People Power Party held an emergency debate at the National Assembly on the 4th titled "The Unconstitutionality of Abolishing Prosecution Supplementary Investigation Rights and the Dismissal of Indictment Clause, and Urging the Exercise of the Presidential Request for Reconsideration" and urged President Lee Jae-myung to exercise his veto over the law abolishing supplementary investigation rights, stating that "abolishing supplementary investigation rights will lead to the downfall of the administration." (국민의힘은 4일 국회에서 ‘검찰 보완수사권 폐지·공소기각 조항의 위헌성과 대통령 재의요구권 행사 촉구’ 긴급 토론회를 열고 “보완수사권 폐지는 정권 폐지로 이어질 것”이라며 이재명 대통령의 보완수사권 폐지법 거부권 행사를 촉구했다.)

Party leader Jang Dong-hyuk attended the debate and said, "The public does not view the exercise of the veto (over the supplementary investigation rights abolition law) as President Lee Jae-myung's choice. They see it as a historic command from the people that must be obeyed." He added, "If this command is defied, the abolition of supplementary investigation rights will ultimately lead to the abolition of the administration." Jang continued, "The victim of the Busan 'kick-back' murder case opened a social media account and desperately appealed for a veto to be exercised over the Criminal Procedure Act amendment," and "Is there anything that better demonstrates the essence of this unjust law than the reality of a citizen who nearly crossed the threshold of death because the state failed to protect them, now crying out to the state to stand on the victim's side?" <<> Rep. Na Kyung-won, who organized the debate, said, "The gates of hell have opened. The Democratic Party pushed through the Criminal Procedure Act amendment that the majority of the public opposes and even the Minister of Justice and the acting Prosecutor General expressed their intention to resign over," and "This is a law passed solely to complete the long-standing narrative of demonizing the prosecution among hardcore supporters and to align with the Democratic Party's leadership race." Rep. Na added, "What's even more problematic is that they quietly slipped in the amendment to Article 327, the grounds for dismissal of indictment," and "They use vague concepts like 'serious' and 'significant,' and claim they merely codified existing Supreme Court precedents, but even that is a misreading of the precedents." She then said, "As you know, the Busan 'kick-back' victim commented, 'Go to hell.' The Democratic Party's claim is not even in line with the late President Roh Moo-hyun's intentions, as Rep. Kwak Sang-eon argued," and "This drives the public into suffering." <<> Rep. Kim Mi-ae also said, "Recently, the police referred Kim Seong-tae, former chairman of Ssangbangwool Group, who handed over donations in connection with the alleged split-donation suspicions, to the prosecution, but decided not to refer Rep. Kang Seon-woo, who allegedly received the donations," and "The prosecution's opportunity to correct such an irrational and contradictory police investigation has now disappeared. With the loss of the checks-and-balances function, powerful criminal suspects gain a sturdy shield, but ordinary citizens and powerless victims are left only with grievance." <<> Rep. Kim said, "At this point, one cannot help but suspect backroom deals behind a bill that 'removes the president's crimes,'" and "If that is not true, President Lee Jae-myung should exercise his veto power under the request for reconsideration." (장동혁 대표는 이날 토론회에 참석해 “국민들은 (보안수사권 폐지법) 거부권 행사가 이재명 대통령의 선택 사항이라 생각하지 않는다. 반드시 거부권을 행사해야만 하는 국민의 역사적 명령이라 생각한다”며 “이 명령을 거역하면 결국 보완수사권 폐지가 정권 폐지로 이어질 것”이라고 했다. 장 대표는 “부산 돌려차기 사건 피해자는 소셜미디어에 계정을 개설해 형소법 개정안에 거부권을 행사해 달라고 절박히 호소했다”며 “국가가 지켜주지 못해 죽음의 문턱까지 갔던 국민이 국가를 향해 피해자의 편이 되어 달라고 절규하는 현실보다 이 악법의 본질을 더 잘 보여주는 게 어디 있겠느냐”고 했다.)

item.title: U.S. Ambassador Steel Calls on Foreign Minister Cho Hyun, Discusses Ways to Advance Korea-U.S. Relations (스틸 美대사, 조현 외교장관 예방… 한미관계 발전방안 논의)
item.description:
U.S. Ambassador to South Korea Michelle Steel officially began her duties on the 4th by submitting a copy of her letter of credence to the Chief of Protocol at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. (미셸 스틸 주한 미국 대사가 4일 외교부 의전장에게 신임장 사본을 제출하며 공식 활동을 시작했다.)

Ambassador Steel arrived at the ministry building that afternoon accompanied by her husband, attorney Sean Steel. Foreign ambassadors newly appointed to South Korea must present the letter of credence, issued by their head of state, to the president of the host country, but before doing so, they submit a copy to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and commence their official activities. (스틸 대사는 이날 오후 남편 숀 스틸 변호사와 함께 외교부 청사에 도착했다. 한국에 새로 부임하는 외국 대사는 자국 국가 원수로부터 받은 신임장을 주재국 대통령에게 제정(提呈)해야 하는데, 그 전에 외교부에 신임장 사본을 제출하고 공식 활동을 시작한다.)

Following the submission of the letter of credence, Ambassador Steel paid a courtesy call on Foreign Minister Cho Hyun. Ministry of Foreign Affairs Spokesperson Park Du-soon stated, "The visit to the minister was for the purpose of a courtesy introduction, and both sides also exchanged views on ways to develop Korea-U.S. relations." (스틸 대사는 신임장 사본 제출에 이어 조현 외교부 장관을 예방했다. 박두순 외교부 대변인은 “이번 장관 예방은 부임 인사를 위한 것으로 양측은 한미 관계 발전 방안에 대해서도 의견을 교환했다”고 말했다.)

Minister Cho and Ambassador Steel are believed to have discussed major issues between Korea and the U.S., including American investment, the Coupang issue, and security consultations. Ambassador Steel did not respond to reporters' questions about what she discussed with Minister Cho. (조 장관과 스틸 대사는 한미 간에 가장 큰 현안인 대미 투자와 쿠팡 문제, 안보 협의 등을 논의한 것으로 보인다. 스틸 대사는 조 장관과 어떤 논의를 했느냐는 취재진 질문에 답하지 않았다.)

Attorney Sean Steel has accompanied Ambassador Steel at all public events since her arrival in Korea on the 30th of last month. It is unusual for an ambassador's spouse to accompany them when submitting the copy of the letter of credence to the ministry, as opposed to the official ceremony for presenting the original document. A ministry official said, "It's somewhat of an exceptional case, but Attorney Steel is a prominent politician who served as chair of the California Republican Party and is known to have extensive networks both inside and outside the Trump administration," adding that this would help build friendly Korea-U.S. relations. (숀 스틸 변호사는 지난달 30일 스틸 대사 입국 때부터 모든 공개 일정에 동행하고 있다. 주한 대사가 신임장 정본을 제정하는 공식 행사가 아닌, 외교부 사본 제출 때 배우자와 동행하는 것은 이례적인 일이다. 외교부 당국자는 “조금 특별한 케이스지만, 스틸 변호사는 캘리포니아주 공화당 의장을 지낸 유력 정치인으로 트럼프 행정부 안팎에 폭넓은 네트워크를 가진 것으로 안다”며 우호적 한미 관계 구축에 도움이 될 것이라고 했다.)

item.title: Government Summons Senior Diplomat Over Japan's Defense White Paper Claiming Dokdo Sovereignty, Urges Withdrawal (정부, ‘독도 영유권 주장’ 日방위백서에 총괄공사 초치 “철회 촉구”)
item.description:
The government has protested and demanded the withdrawal of Japan's Defense White Paper, released on the 4th, which describes Dokdo as Japanese territory. (정부는 일본 정부가 4일 발표한 방위백서에 독도를 자국의 고유 영토라고 표현한 데 대해 항의하고 철회를 촉구했다.)

Park Doo-soon, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said at a regular briefing that day, "The government strongly protests Japan's repeated unjust sovereignty claims over Dokdo, which is clearly our inherent territory historically, geographically, and under international law, as stated in its Defense White Paper, and urges its immediate withdrawal." (박두순 외교부 대변인은 이날 정례 브리핑에서 “정부는 일본 정부가 방위백서를 통해 역사적·지리적·국제법적으로 명백한 우리 고유 영토인 독도에 대해 부당한 영유권 주장을 되풀이한 데 대해 강력히 항의하며 이를 즉각 철회할 것을 촉구한다”고 말했다.)

He added, "We make it clear once again that Japan's unjust claims have no impact whatsoever on our sovereignty over Dokdo, and we state that we will respond firmly to any provocation by Japan regarding Dokdo." (이어 “일본 정부의 부당한 주장이 독도에 대한 우리 주권에 아무런 영향도 미치지 못한다는 점을 다시 한번 분명히 하며, 독도에 대한 일본의 어떠한 도발에 대해서도 단호하게 대응할 것임을 밝힌다”고 했다.)

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs summoned Kazuo Chujo, chief minister at the Japanese Embassy in South Korea, that day to convey its protest. Chujo left the ministry building without answering reporters' questions, including "What did you discuss?" and "Why does Japan repeat its sovereignty claims over Dokdo while calling South Korea an important partner?" (외교부는 이날 추조 가즈오 주한 일본 대사관 총괄공사를 초치해 항의의 뜻을 전달했다. 추조 공사는 ‘어떤 이야기를 나눴느냐’, ‘한국이 중요한 파트너라면서 독도 영유권 주장을 반복하는 이유가 무엇인가’ 등의 취재진 질문에 아무 대답을 하지 않고 외교부 청사를 빠져나갔다.)

The Ministry of National Defense also summoned Takeshi Nagayoshi, Japan's defense attaché in South Korea, to its office that afternoon, where Kim Hak-jo, director general for international policy, lodged a protest and urged immediate correction and cessation of such actions in the future. (국방부도 이날 오후 김학조 국제정책관이 나가요시 다케시 주한 일본 방위주재관을 청사로 초치해 항의하고, 즉각 시정할 것과 향후 이런 행위를 중단할 것을 촉구했다.)

In this year's Defense White Paper, released after a cabinet meeting that day, the Japanese government stated, "The territorial issues of the Northern Territories (the Japanese term for the four Kuril Islands) and Takeshima (the Japanese name for Dokdo), which are inherent territories of our country (Japan), remain unresolved." Japan has claimed sovereignty over Dokdo in its Defense White Paper for 22 consecutive years since 2005. (일본 정부는 이날 각의(국무회의) 이후 발표한 올해 방위백서에서 “우리나라(일본) 고유 영토인 북방 영토(쿠릴 4개 섬의 일본식 표현)와 다케시마(竹島·일본이 주장하는 독도 명칭) 영토 문제가 여전히 미해결 상태로 존재한다”고 적었다. 일본은 방위백서에서 2005년 이후 22년 연속으로 독도 영유권을 주장하고 있다.)

item.title: Han Dong-hoon: "Abolition of Supplementary Investigation Rights Opens the Gates of Hell" (한동훈 “보완수사권 폐지, 지옥문 열렸다”)
item.description:
Independent lawmaker Han Dong-hoon said on the 4th, regarding the "Supplementary Investigation Abolition Act" that passed the National Assembly led by the Democratic Party of Korea and also passed the Cabinet meeting, "The gates of hell have opened for crime victims and all citizens of the Republic of Korea." (한동훈 무소속 의원은 4일 더불어민주당 주도로 국회를 통과한 ‘보완수사 폐지법이 국무회의도 통과한 것과 관련해 “범죄 피해자와 대한민국 국민 모두에게 지옥문이 열렸다”고 했다.)

At an emergency briefing held that afternoon at the National Assembly alongside Kim Jin-ju (pseudonym), a victim of the "Busan spinning kick" case, Han said, "The people will now reject President Lee Jae-myung, who has mortgaged the entire nation just to win one party leadership election." He added, "Abolishing supplementary investigation rights is a declaration to side with murderers like Jang Yun-gi and criminals like the spinning kick perpetrator." (한 의원은 이날 오후 국회에서 ‘부산 돌려차기 사건’ 피해자인 김진주씨(가명)와 함께 ‘보완수사 금지, 지옥문이 열렸다’ 긴급 간담회를 열고 “(민주당) 전당대회 한번 이겨보겠다고 전 국민을 근저당 잡은 이재명 대통령을 이제 국민이 거부할 것”이라고 했다. 그는 “(보완수사권 폐지는) 장윤기 같은 살인자 편, 돌려차기 범인 같은 범죄자의 편을 들겠다고 선언한 것”이라고 했다.)

Lawmaker Park Jeong-hoon, who attended the briefing, targeted the Democratic Party, saying, "Destroying the national judicial system to maintain their own power is a serious criminal act that politics can commit in constitutional history." (간담회에 참석한 박정훈 의원은 민주당을 겨냥해 “자신들의 권력을 유지하기 위해 국가 사법시스템을 무너뜨린 건 헌정사에서 정치가 저지를 수 있는 심각한 범죄행위”라고 했다.)

Kim Jin-ju, the victim of the spinning kick case, said, "Among victims, some are anxious about whether they have to undergo ping-pong investigations, and others express unease about whether their trials will end before the prosecution's work does. Even at this moment, there are no protective measures for victims." (돌려차기 사건 피해자인 김진주씨는 “피해자 중에 핑퐁 수사를 받아야 하는지 불안해하는 분들도 있고, 자기 재판이 검찰이 끝나기 전에 끝날지 불안감을 호소하는 분도 있다”며 " 지금 이 시점에도 피해자들에 대한 장치는 아무것도 없다”고 했다.)

Regarding President Lee's remarks at the Cabinet meeting that day, in which he suggested it was "hard to see the Criminal Procedure Act amendment as unconstitutional," Kim said, "I'm so angry my hands are shaking. He's an evasive president. Crime victims are in hell right now, and instead of saying whether he supports or opposes it, he just says it doesn't violate the Constitution—that means he doesn't want to bear the heavy responsibility." (김씨는 이 대통령이 이날 국무회의에서 ‘형사소송법 개정안이 위헌이라고 보기 힘들다’는 취지로 발언한 것과 관련해선 “화가 너무 많이 나서 손이 떨린다. 회피형 대통령”이라며 “범죄 피해자들은 지금 지옥에 있는데, 본인이 지지한다 반대한다 이야기도 하지 않고 헌법에 위반되지 않는다고 하는 건 막중한 책임을 지기 싫다는 것”이라고 했다.)
